message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each 1‑9, one 0) and two of each action card: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score **500 points** (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied at the end of each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you may play **one** card that matches the discard pile’s **color**, **number**, or **action**. 3. If you can’t play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. | | **Wild Draw Four Rules** | You may only play it if you have **no other playable card** (i.e., you cannot match the current color or number). If challenged and you were wrong, you must draw 4 cards instead of the opponent drawing 4. | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your **second‑to‑last** card, you must say “UNO” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score. | | **Optional Variations** | • **Stacking** – allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards on top of each other.
• **Custom Decks** – add extra action cards or themed cards.
• **House Rules** – e.g., “Draw Two on a Skip” or “Reverse on a Wild.” | --- ### Quick Play‑through Example 1. **Setup**: 4 players. Each gets 7 cards. Top card of draw pile is a Red 5 → discard pile starts with Red 5. 2. **Player 1** (clockwise) has a Red 9 → plays it. 3. **Player 2** has a Green 9 → cannot play (must match color or number). Draws a card; it’s a Yellow 9 → plays it. 4. **Player 3** has a Yellow Skip → plays it. Player 4 skips a turn. 5. **Player 1** now must play a Yellow card or a Skip/Draw Two. They play a Yellow 2. 6. ... and so on until someone empties their hand. --- ### Tips for New Players - **Keep an eye on colors** – try to hold onto a variety of colors so you’re not stuck. - **Use Wilds strategically** – change the color when you’re about to run out of matching cards. - **Watch for “UNO”** – it’s a quick way to avoid penalties. - **Remember the stack rule** (if you’re playing it) – you can chain Draw Twos or Wild Draw Fours to protect yourself. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
